items.title: Cosa c’entra l’Eritrea con il conflitto in Etiopia
items.summary: La presenza dei soldati di Asmara in Tigrai, l’ambizione etiope di ottenere un accesso al mare, il ruolo strategico del mar Rosso. Come sta evolvendo la guerra, secondo i giornali stranieri Leggi
items.content:
Anche questa settimana giornaliste, analisti ed esperti del continente africano hanno concentrato la loro attenzione sul Corno d’Africa per osservare le dinamiche messe in moto dall’inizio di una nuova guerra nella regione etiope del Tigrai. Il timore principale è che un conflitto prevalentemente interno (le forze del governo di Abiy Ahmed contro una coalizione di gruppi armati, ognuno con una forte connotazione regionale) si trasformi in uno scontro più ampio, in grado di diffondersi nel resto della regione coinvolgendo altri paesi, primo tra tutti l’Eritrea.

L’Etiopia, che la settimana scorsa ha rotto i rapporti diplomatici con il paese vicino (alleato invece nella precedente guerra in Tigrai del 2020-2022), accusa Asmara di sostenere i ribelli. Del pericolo di un allargamento del conflitto ha parlato al podcast Il Mondo la corrispondente della Reuters in Africa subsahariana, Giulia Paravicini, che di recente ha pubblicato un reportage dall’Eritrea, dove i giornalisti stranieri difficilmente riescono a entrare.

L’8 ottobre diverse fonti giornalistiche (tra cui la Reuters e la Bbc ) hanno confermato la presenza delle truppe eritree nel nord dell’Etiopia, in particolare nella città di Adigrat, dove è stato avvistato un convoglio formato da decine di camion. Il giorno successivo è arrivata anche la notizia che i soldati eritrei sono stati il bersaglio di attacchi con i droni sferrati dalle forze del governo etiope. Tutti eventi che danno sostanza al timore di una diffusione regionale degli scontri.

Subito dopo l’ascesa al potere del premier etiope Abiy Ahmed, nel 2018, Etiopia ed Eritrea avevano chiuso un lungo contenzioso e il successo diplomatico era valso ad Abiy il premio Nobel per la pace. Ma, dopo aver combattuto fianco a fianco contro il Fronte popolare di liberazione del Tigrai (Tplf) nell’ultima guerra, Asmara e Addis Abeba si sono trovate di nuovo ai ferri corti.

In primo luogo, perché Asmara non era stata coinvolta nell’accordo di pace di Pretoria che aveva messo fine a quel conflitto; poi, perché Abiy – non contento di quanto avuto finora dal suo governo – mira a ottenere uno sbocco sul mare per il suo paese di 130 milioni di abitanti. E uno dei porti più vicini è quello di Assab, in Eritrea.

“L’Eritrea occupa un vasto territorio in una delle aree più calde del momento”, ha detto Murithi Mutiga, dell’International crisis group, alla Reuters. Asmara ha infatti il controllo di una costa lunga mille chilometri sul mar Rosso, via di passaggio per gli scambi commerciali, diventata ancora più importante dopo la chiusura dello stretto di Hormuz a causa della guerra in Iran.

Queste coste fanno gola ad Abiy, spiega un lungo articolo del sito egiziano Mada Masr . Nell’articolo Faisal Ali, Hassan Alnaser, Hazem Tharwat e Kidus Lemma scrivono che la ricerca di un accesso al mare fa parte di una strategia più ampia dell’Etiopia per ricostruire la sua posizione regionale.

Per questo Abiy cerca una soluzione stabile, e non accordi di breve termine, come quello proposto dal Somaliland nel 2024, in cui il governo di Hargeisa ha offerto ad Addis Abeba di prendere in affitto venti chilometri di costa intorno al porto di Berbera, con tutto quello che ne consegue per i paesi vicini. Tra l’altro, l’idea che il governo del Somaliland disponga in questo modo del territorio sotto il suo controllo non va giù alle autorità di Mogadiscio, che rivendicano la sovranità somala su quelle terre.

Simile è la lettura di Ishaan Tharoor sul New Yorker , che fa il punto sulle alleanze regionali (ricapitolando: da una parte possiamo mettere Egitto, Sudan, Eritrea e Somalia, che in qualche modo si portano dietro anche Turchia e Qatar; dall’altra, Etiopia, Emirati Arabi Uniti, Forze di supporto rapido sudanesi, Somaliland e in una certa misura anche Israele. Attraverso le parole di una delle sue fonti, Tharoor descrive il Corno d’Africa come “una parte disfunzionale della già frammentata scena politica del Medio Oriente”.

Infine, per approfondire la politica degli Stati Uniti nella regione, segnalo su Semafor una breve analisi firmata da Cameron Hudson, secondo cui Washington ha già scelto chi sostenere: l’Etiopia, paese che meglio s’inserisce nella “diplomazia commerciale” del segretario di stato Marco Rubio. Ma, secondo Hudson, per gli Stati Uniti è un errore, perché perdono la possibilità di fare da mediatore tra il governo e i ribelli.

Internazionale pubblica ogni settimana una pagina di lettere. Ci piacerebbe sapere cosa pensi di questo articolo. Scrivici a: posta@internazionale.it

items.title: Le nuove tecnologie danno dipendenza?
items.summary: Le nuove tecnologie danno dipendenza?
items.content:
Alcuni scommettono in Borsa prima ancora di essere diventati maggiorenni con il trading online, anche se sarebbe illegale. Altri non muovono un passo senza aver consultato ChatGPT o Gemini, poco importa se sugli affari di cuore o sul compito in classe. Tantissimi passano ore e ore sui social, ipnotizzati da reel e foto, senza concentrarsi su nulla per più di qualche secondo.
È la realtà di molti adolescenti italiani, ma guai a pensare che gli adulti siano immuni: la rivoluzione del Web ha travolto anche chi ha trascorso la prima parte della vita in un mondo analogico e ora per tutti, a ogni età, lo spettro della dipendenza da Internet, smartphone e social non è così remoto.. Evolutivamente vulnerabili
Il tempo vola, scrollando video al cellulare: a tutti capita di stare col telefono in mano un'ora, credendo che siano passati pochi minuti. Qualcuno pensa a quello fin dal risveglio al mattino: scivolare nella dipendenza da nuove tecnologie è facile, perché come ha spiegato di recente Keith Humphreys, psichiatra dell'Università di Stanford in California (Usa), in un documento sulle dipendenze: «Abbiamo un cervello antico in un ambiente nuovo. La vulnerabilità alle dipendenze non ha avuto conseguenze per il 99,9% della nostra evoluzione. Ora però tutto ciò che ha un grande potenziale per indurle, dalle sostanze alle tecnologie, è a portata di mano».. Per le nuove dipendenze - da Internet, social, giochi d'azzardo e così via - valgono infatti meccanismi simili a quelli che portano a non poter più fare a meno delle sostanze d'abuso: slot machine e media digitali sono disegnati apposta per farci provare picchi di piacere, e così l'abitudine a stare collegati, vedere serie Tv o "parlare" con un'intelligenza artificiale si trasforma in dipendenza.. Un vero disturbo mentale
«Le dipendenze comportamentali sono un vero disturbo del sistema nervoso centrale», spiega Massimo Clerici, presidente della sezione di Psichiatria delle dipendenze della Società italiana di psichiatria. «Non esistono però precisi criteri diagnostici per le dipendenze comportamentali, fatta eccezione per il gioco d'azzardo o online (gaming), che ne è spesso diretta conseguenza ed è inserito nella Classificazione internazionale delle malattie dell'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità».
Tutto il resto, dallo shopping compulsivo all'uso problematico di Internet, non è ancora ben definito ma è ormai ben presente nell'esperienza di tanti, a partire dai giovanissimi. Secondo i risultati del progetto "Generazione Z 2.0", del Centro nazionale dipendenze e doping dell'Istituto superiore di sanità, in Italia circa 15.000 studenti fra gli 11 e i 13 anni non riescono a staccarsi dai social. Altri 111.000 sono a rischio di disturbo da gaming e 87.000 hanno comportamenti di gioco d'azzardo a rischio o problematici.. Non va meglio al crescere dell'età: stando ai dati raccolti nel 2025 per lo studio Espad (European school Survey Project on Alcohol and other Drugs, coordinato in Italia dall'Istituto di Fisiologia Clinica del Cnr), quasi 370.000 ragazzi fra i 15 e i 19 anni trascurano sonno e relazioni per navigare sul Web e diventano intrattabili se manca la connessione, e altri 380.000 giocano troppo online. I numeri sono in crescita costante ed è emersa pure la nuova tendenza delle scommesse in Borsa: oltre 420.000 under 18 hanno provato almeno una volta.. I rischi per i ragazzini
«Questi numeri raccontano un problema sociale, ma le nuove dipendenze hanno ricadute biologiche e cliniche altrettanto rilevanti», puntualizza Clerici. «La sovrabbondanza di stimoli da nuove tecnologie, anche apparentemente non dannosi, può avere conseguenze negative sullo sviluppo cognitivo ed emotivo. La riduzione del sonno negli adolescenti, che di notte restano svegli su Internet e social, si associa a un maggior rischio di depressione e ansia. E si sta anche osservando che l'uso intensivo dei social da parte dei giovanissimi altera il funzionamento di alcune aree cerebrali».
Marco Potenza, psichiatra dell'Università di Yale (Usa) che studia da tempo gli effetti delle nuove tecnologie sullo sviluppo di bambini e adolescenti, ha sottolineato su Current Addiction Report che nei più piccoli si possono modificare le connessioni cerebrali e si può interferire con lo sviluppo del linguaggio. Anche che la facilità di accesso a contenuti pornografici in età prepuberale e adolescenziale può avere ricadute sugli equilibri ormonali, col rischio di alterare la maturazione sessuale, anticipandola.. Contenuti mirati e vulnerabilità
«I social poi sono realizzati in modo da agganciare i ragazzi in base a età e sesso, per proporre contenuti selezionati», riprende Clerici. «Ai giovani vengono indirizzati spesso contenuti relativi all'immagine, in un momento in cui il corpo cambia e quindi si è sensibili a questi temi». La dipendenza da social e da Internet quindi si può così trasformare in problemi clinici assai concreti, dall'anoressia fino alla cosmeticoressia (la fissazione per trucchi e skincare).. «Non tutti sviluppano patologie correlate alle nuove dipendenze; alcuni sono più vulnerabili per fattori familiari o biologici o anche per traumi pregressi», dice Clerici. Uno studio italiano dell'Università di Messina su quasi 700 studenti delle superiori, per esempio, ha sottolineato che il rischio di un utilizzo problematico dello smartphone è maggiore in chi ha tratti riconducibili al disturbo dell'attenzione e iperattività.
«Non abbiamo purtroppo farmaci per le dipendenze comportamentali; si può solo intervenire per gestire i sintomi valutandone la gravità, l'intensità e quanto incidono sulla vita quotidiana», specifica Clerici.. Campanelli d'allarme
Cogliere i segni di un uso problematico della tecnologia è quindi fondamentale. Possono destare sospetti: il pensiero continuo e il desiderio estremo di utilizzare smartphone o computer per accedere ai contenuti, le bugie a parenti e amici sulla realtà del proprio utilizzo della tecnologia, le lunghe ore trascorse in rete, le conseguenze nella vita reale, come problemi di relazione e disturbi fisici (mal di testa, irritazioni oculari ecc.).
Un'auto-analisi onesta per capire se si sta esagerando aiuta gli adulti, ma con i figli serve il dialogo: «Una relazione attenta è importante, ma non è detto che basti: anche se a casa e a scuola si parla dei rischi delle nuove tecnologie, da fuori arrivano stimoli potentissimi», osserva Clerici. «Normare l'accesso alle tecnologie da parte dei minori del resto è difficile e pensare di rallentarlo è un'illusione. Quel che si può fare è avere le antenne dritte e non ignorare i segnali: se un figlio sta collegato per ore è opportuno provare a capire di quali contenuti fruisce e che cosa fa online»..

items.title: US country music star Ella Langley cancels show due to 'security threat'
items.summary: Police say they checked the concert venue in Tulsa, Oklahoma but "could not find any threat".
items.content:
US country music star Ella Langley has said she had to cancel her sold-out concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma on Friday night, due to a "serious security threat".

The singer made what she called the "incredibly difficult" decision around two hours before the show at the 19,000-seater arena was due to start.

In a post on Instagram, the 27-year-old said the threat involved "the safety of my fans, the venue staff and my team".

Cpt Richard Meulenberg from Tulsa Police Department said a person had called saying "great harm" would be done at the event with "shots fired and bombs."

He stated his team had checked the venue at BOK Center several times before the show and "could not find any threat".

"The event was ready to go," he added, saying officers with sniffer dogs did a sweep of the arena again after the phone call was made.

"We could not find a credible threat," he said, stressing that the person who had made the call "disrupted this entire event" for thousands of Langley fans.

The star - who did not give any further details - also apologised to her fans, saying additional information regarding ticket refunds "will be shared as soon as possible".

BOK Center issued its own statement, saying that "the safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed.

"We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologise to fans who planned to attend."

In September, Langley's country smash Choosin' Texas overtook Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You to become the longest-running number one single in US chart history.

Its success helped the singer from Alabama to sweep the Academy of Country Music Awards in May.

items.title: Smetti di pagare il cloud ogni mese: ecco i NAS UGREEN scontati per la Festa delle Offerte Prime
items.summary: Lo sai quanto spenderai in abbonamenti cloud negli anni in cui custodirai i tuoi documenti e le tue foto? Con un NAS paghi una volta sola, e dal 6 all'11 ottobre UGREEN ha in sconto sei dispositivi ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dal 6 ottobre Amazon apre la Festa delle Offerte Prime, 48 ore di sconti riservati agli abbonati Prime, e UGREEN concentra in questi due giorni i ribassi più alti della sua promozione d'autunno sui NAS NASync : sei modelli scontati sia su Amazon sia sul sito del produttore.

Un NAS (Network Attached Storage) collega al router uno o più hard disk e li rende raggiungibili da telefoni, computer e televisori, sia sulla rete di casa sia da fuori tramite Internet.

Il secondo argomento riguarda il controllo dei dati, poiché foto, documenti e backup restano sui dischi di casa e non passano dai server di terzi.

Per tutti i NASync è presente la cifratura delle connessioni con TLS/SSL, RSA e AES , l'autenticazione a due fattori e un Security Manager che controlla il sistema in modo continuo. I NAS hanno ottenuto anche la certificazione di sicurezza ETSI EN 303 645, rilasciata da TÜV SÜD, e quella statunitense TRUSTe. Anche il riconoscimento dei volti e degli oggetti nell'app Foto gira sul NAS senza inviare le immagini a servizi esterni.

C'è poi la velocità. Dentro casa i trasferimenti dipendono dalla rete locale e non dalla linea internet in upload, che nelle connessioni domestiche resta di solito il collo di bottiglia, specialmente se non si ha una fibra seria. Su una porta a 2,5 Gb/s si arriva a un massimo teorico di 312,5 MB/s, che vuol dire copiare un video 4K da 20 GB in poco più di un minuto.

È facile anche la configurazione, che sui NAS UGREEN richiede meno di dieci minuti e un'unica app per gestire file, backup delle foto e streaming verso la TV.

La prima decisione riguarda il numero di alloggiamenti per i dischi . Con due dischi si può impostare il RAID 1, che scrive gli stessi dati su entrambi: se un disco si guasta, i file restano sull'altro, ma la capienza utile è alla fine quella di un solo disco perché il secondo serve come sicurezza. Con quattro o sei alloggiamenti si possono usare il RAID 5 e il RAID 6, che salvano su tutti i dischi anche delle informazioni di controllo; quindi se un disco si rompe (due, con il RAID 6), il NAS ricostruisce i file mancanti a partire da quelli rimasti.

Conviene pensare a quanto crescerà l'archivio nei prossimi anni, perché quando tutti gli alloggiamenti saranno occupati, per avere più spazio bisognerà sostituire i dischi con altri più capienti, uno alla volta, oppure collegare un'unità esterna. Partire con un NAS a quattro alloggiamenti e due soli dischi lascia invece margine per aggiungerne altri due in seguito.

La seconda riguarda il processore. I modelli della serie DH di UGREEN usano chip ARM di Rockchip, poco energivori e sufficienti per archivio, backup e streaming , con una versione semplificata del sistema operativo UGOS Pro e memoria non espandibile.

La serie DXP monta processori Intel, ha la versione completa di UGOS Pro, memoria espandibile e due slot M.2 per SSD da usare come cache o come spazio aggiuntivo. È quindi la strada per chi vuole affiancare all'archivio carichi più pesanti , come le macchine virtuali o un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, oppure servire molti utenti insieme.

La terza e ultima scelta è quella della rete . Una porta da 1 Gb/s basta per foto e documenti, quella da 2,5 Gb/s è utile con i video pesanti, mentre i 10 Gb/s servono a chi lavora in rete su file di grandi dimensioni e ha computer e switch in grado di sfruttarli.

Il DH2300 è pensato per chi un NAS non l'ha mai avuto e vuole soprattutto mettere al sicuro le foto di famiglia, smettendo di rincorrere lo spazio libero sul telefono. Ha due alloggiamenti: con due dischi in RAID 1 ogni file viene salvato due volte e, se uno dei dischi si guasta, l'archivio resta intatto. Si configura dall'app UGREEN con una procedura guidata e, per collegare lo smartphone, basta avvicinarlo al NAS grazie all'NFC .

Collegato al televisore del salotto tramite l'uscita HDMI 4K, riproduce film e video di casa senza bisogno di un computer . Il processore Rockchip a otto core e i 4 GB di memoria bastano per archivio, backup e streaming, con una capienza che arriva a 64 TB complessivi.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DH2300, da listino di 246,99 euro, scende a 189,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Quando i dispositivi da salvare diventano tanti, tra gli smartphone di tutta la famiglia, i portatili e magari il lavoro da casa, due dischi si riempiono in fretta. Il DH4300 Plus raddoppia gli alloggiamenti, fino a 128 TB, e permette di scegliere il RAID 5 o il RAID 6 , che proteggono i dati sacrificando meno spazio.

La porta di rete a 2,5 Gb/s accorcia i tempi quando si salvano video pesanti, e il processore Rockchip RK3588C con 8 GB di memoria regge più persone collegate insieme. Chi ha un po' di dimestichezza può installare applicazioni aggiuntive tramite Docker , mentre per tutti gli altri restano la configurazione guidata e l'app unica del DH2300.

Nei giorni della Festa delle Offerte Prime, e fino all'11 ottobre, il prezzo scende da 439,99 euro a 319,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP4800 Plus è il modello per chi dal NAS vuole qualcosa in più di un archivio , quindi un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, qualche macchina virtuale, i backup automatici di tutti i computer di casa o dello studio.

Il processore Intel Pentium Gold a cinque core lavora con 8 GB di memoria DDR5, espandibili fino a 64 GB, e il sistema gira su un SSD dedicato da 128 GB.

Accanto ai quattro alloggiamenti per hard disk ci sono due slot per SSD M.2 , da usare come cache per velocizzare i file aperti più spesso con una capienza massima di 144 TB.

La porta da 10 Gb/s, affiancata da una seconda a 2,5 Gb/s, serve a chi lavora su file grandi da un computer collegato via cavo, e il lettore di schede SD permette di scaricare le foto della fotocamera direttamente sul NAS.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il prezzo scende da 729,99 euro a 549,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con sei alloggiamenti per hard disk e due per SSD, il DXP6800 Pro si rivolge a un piccolo studio professionale o a chi custodisce un archivio video di anni perché può arrivare fino a 208 TB di spazio.

Il processore Intel Core i5 a dieci core permette a più persone di lavorare contemporaneamente sugli stessi file, anche mentre il NAS esegue i backup o converte un video.

Le due porte di rete da 10 Gb/s si possono unire fino a 20 Gb/s , e le due Thunderbolt 4 servono a collegare dischi esterni veloci, per esempio per scaricare il materiale di una giornata di riprese. L 'uscita HDMI arriva fino all'8K.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DXP6800 Pro è in offerta, passando dal listino di 1.209,99 euro a 899,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP2800 è per chi si accontenta di due dischi ma dal NAS vuole più di un archivio di foto. Ha gli stessi due alloggiamenti del DH2300, ma monta un processore Intel più potente e la versione completa del sistema UGOS Pro , con più applicazioni a disposizione. La memoria si può ampliare fino a 16 GB e due slot per SSD servono a velocizzare i file usati più spesso.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre si scende dal listino di 439,99 euro a 329,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP480T Plus rinuncia agli hard disk e accoglie quattro SSD M.2 NVMe , così da lavorare sui file video direttamente dalla rete senza rallentamenti. Monta lo stesso Core i5 del DXP6800 Pro, una porta da 10 Gb/s e due Thunderbolt 4.

In questo caso lo sconto vale solo il 6 e 7 ottobre: in quei due giorni il prezzo di listino di 999,99 euro passa a 749,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con la Festa delle Offerte Prime è il momento giusto per smettere di pagare lo spazio online ogni mese e riportare a casa i propri ricordi, una volta per tutte.

Sui NAS UGREEN i prezzi della festa restano validi dal 6 fino all'11 ottobre su tutti i modelli tranne il DXP480T Plus, che sale dal prezzo scontato di 749,99 euro a 899,99 euro già dall'8 ottobre. Tutte le offerte sono sulla pagina UGREEN di Amazon e sulla pagina dedicata del sito UGREEN .

items.summary: Dodici modelli scontati fino al 31 ottobre, dai Combo d'ingresso ai Max con la base che lava il rullo. E dall'8 ottobre sei robot in offerta anche su Amazon ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Per tutto ottobre il negozio online di iRobot mette in offerta 12 modelli dei suoi Roomb a , dal Roomba Combo 105 a 149 euro fino al prestanti Roomba Max 775 Combo con base AutoWash. Da oggi e fino al 31 ottobre, 6 modelli sono scontati anche su Amazon , in qualche caso a un prezzo ancora più basso. Se c'era un momento per smettere di passare l'aspirapolvere e il mocio, è questo.

Dodici voci possono spaventare, ma il listino si legge bene se lo si guarda per famiglie. Salendo di prezzo, il robot si prende in carico lavori che altrimenti resterebbero a noi, come svuotare il contenitore della polvere e lavare i panni sporchi. Scegliere significa anche capire fin dove si vuole delegare.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo, cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con ClearView LiDAR , un sensore laser che misura le stanze e ne disegna la mappa. Il robot pulisce così per traiettorie ordinate , sa dove è già passato e nell'app si possono indicare le stanze da pulire.

La differenza vera la fa la base di ricarica. Quella AutoEmpty aspira a sua volta lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e va sostituito ogni tre mesi circa. La base AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

Un ultimo dato che può aiutare a orientarsi è la potenza di aspirazione. Si misura in pascal (Pa) , l'unità con cui si esprime la depressione creata dal motore: più il numero è alto, più il robot tira su sporco dai tappeti e dalle fughe . Nei modelli in offerta si va dai 7.000 Pa del 105 ai 30.000 Pa delle fasce più alte.

Il prezzo più basso del mese è quello del Roomba Combo 105 , a 149 euro, o 179 euro con base AutoEmpty . Anche il modello d'ingresso

Con pochi euro in più si entra nella nuova generazione. Il Roomba 115 Combo , nero o bianco, costa 169 euro è più piccolo della precedente generazione 105 in ogni dimensione : 24,5 centimetri di lato contro 33,6 e 9,2 di altezza contro 10,4, per appena 2,16 kg. Così si infila sotto più mobili, e intanto aspira con 15.000 Pa . La spazzola laterale pulisce a filo parete e anche il suo panno in microfibra si stacca e si lava. Con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Ha la navigazione ClearView LiDAR e per il lavaggio usa un panno in microfibra, bagnato da una micropompa con tre livelli d'acqua da scegliere in base al pavimento. Quando riconosce un tappeto, la funzione Carpet Detect lo evita per non bagnarlo . Dall'app Roomba Home si impostano le routine e si sceglie quali stanze pulire per prime.

È uno dei prodotti di punta dell'offerta, e si capisce perché. Il Roomba 115 Combo con base AutoEmpty costa 219 euro e porta lo svuotamento automatico nella fascia d'ingresso.

Il robot è lo stesso 115 appena visto. La base però cambia l'uso quotidiano: a fine pulizia il Roomba rientra, la base aspira lo sporco dal contenitore e per circa tre mesi non serve toccarlo . Chi ha animali in casa, o chi semplicemente non vuole ritrovarsi ogni sera a svuotare un contenitore pieno di polvere, ha qui il modo più economico di dimenticarsene. È in vendita, nero o bianco, allo stesso prezzo.

Con la serie Plus 400 e 500 arriva la base AutoWash , e con lei un design più basso. I tre modelli sono alti appena 8,35 cm , con un profilo più sottile del 21% rispetto al Plus 505 della generazione precedente. In pratica passano più facilmente sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi, dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata.

Il lavaggio è affidato a due panni rotanti DualClean , che girano a 200 giri al minuto. La tecnologia SmartScrub aumenta la pressione sul pavimento contro lo sporco più ostinato , e quando il robot riconosce un tappeto solleva i panni di un centimetro per non bagnarlo.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash costa 349 euro e aspira con 20.000 Pa. Il Roomba Plus 515 Combo + AutoWash sale a 22.000 Pa e costa 399 euro. Entrambi sono disponibili neri o bianchi. Chi cerca la generazione precedente trova invece, sempre con base AutoWash , il Roomba Plus 405 Combo a 299 euro e il Plus 505 Combo a 399 euro.

Il secondo prodotto di punta del mese è il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash , a 449 euro. Nero o bianco, conserva lo stesso profilo basso dei fratelli ma alza ogni dato.

L'aspirazione arriva a 25.000 Pa. La navigazione passa a ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi, scarpe e oggetti lasciati in giro, e li aggira invece di trascinarli. Anche la base fa un passo avanti: lava i panni con acqua a 75 °C e li asciuga con aria calda , così non restano umidi nella base fino al giro successivo, evitando muffe e cattivi odori.

Nella fascia alta cambia il modo di lavare, perché al posto dei panni rotanti c'è un rullo PowerSpin che strofina il pavimento con acqua calda a 60 °C e si pulisce da solo mentre lavora , premendo sul pavimento con una forza di 15 newton. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, usano la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI già vista sul 575 e sono alti 9,95 centimetri.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo , a 549 euro in nero, è la scelta di chi vuole il rullo lavapavimenti spendendo meno. La sua base Wash Only lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga, ma non svuota la polvere , che finisce in un sacchetto da un litro integrato nel robot, sufficiente per circa un mese.

Rispetto al 615 cambia la base, ed è la differenza che si sente di più. La AutoWash svuota la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa da sola il detergente . Si va avanti fino a 90 giorni senza interventi .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash è il terzo prodotto di punta del mese. Costa 599 euro ed è disponibile bianco o nero.

Sul robot la tecnologia PerfectEdge allunga il rullo verso i bordi per arrivare fino al battiscopa , e la spazzola anti-groviglio non resta avvolta dai peli degli animali (ha un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira, così non c'è da liberarla a mano con le forbici).

La serie Max è quella pensata per le case più movimentate, con bambini, animali e tanti tappeti. In offerta c'è il Roomba Max 705 Combo + AutoWash , bianco, a 599 euro. Lava con il rullo PowerSpin già visto sui Plus 615 e 675, protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti mentre il robot li attraversa, e aspira con 13.000 Pa e due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio. La funzione Dirt Detect riconosce le zone più sporche , mentre Carpet Boost alza in automatico la potenza quando il robot sale su un tappeto .

Con PrecisionVision AI il 705 riconosce cavi e calzini, e perfino i bisogni degli animali domestici , e li aggira.

La base AutoWash lava e asciuga il rullo con acqua e aria calde , dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere per 75 giorni.

Chi ha soprattutto tappeti e non ha bisogno del lavaggio può guardare al Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , a 449 euro in nero. È un aspirapolvere puro, con 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect, Carpet Boost e la base AutoEmpty.

L'ultimo prodotto di punta è il modello più completo dell'offerta. Il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash costa 699 euro.

Riunisce quello che si è visto fin qui e si presenta come il più complet o. Aspira con 30.000 Pa, ha le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost degli altri Max, e lava con il rullo PowerSpin, protetto dalla stessa copertura per i tappeti. La base AutoWash svuota lo sporco fino a tre mesi, lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C, dosa il detergente e rabbocca l'acqua . La navigazione è ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, come sul 705.

Da oggi, 6 Roomba sono in offerta anche su Amazon, con prezzi in qualche caso più bassi di quelli di irobot.it. Tra questi ci sono le versioni 416, 516 e 576: sono le versioni proposte su Amazon dei Plus 415, 515 e 575, con le stesse caratteristiche tecniche.

items.title: REA Reverse – Engineer Anything
items.summary: Article URL: https://rea.tools/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50028275 Points: 473 # Comments: 190
items.content:
REA gives your agent the tools to inspect a program and explain what it does.

› Install REA and connect it to this coding agent using npx rea-agents@latest setup. Show me the setup plan for approval, then verify the installation.

Finding out how software works by examining the program itself.

The goal: understand a feature well enough to explain it , change it or rebuild it.

Let's try two examples. Change a game's speed, then return to Calculator and rebuild its % button.

The script actually running in the page. The agent reads its update function and speed settings, then uses that rule in a new game.

› Use REA to inspect this dinosaur game. Why does it get faster? Show the speed rule, then build a small version with an adjustable speed.

Inspected target: wayou’s Chromium-derived browser edition .

Start at 6. Add 0.001 each update without a collision, while speed is below 13 .

REA inspected the HTTP browser edition through a local debugging connection and returned the loaded index.js , including its source and digest.

We called the original game’s update function in a controlled browser check, with obstacles and automatic scheduling disabled. After 4,000 updates, speed was 10.0; after 10,000, it was 13.0, rounded to one decimal.

The new mini-game keeps that speed rule. Its drawing, jumping and collision code are a small teaching implementation. Open the lab to see the new code and run the same speed check.

To inspect the target yourself, follow the browser connection steps using the dinosaur page . Give your agent that page URL and your local debugging endpoint, then copy the prompt above.

We saw why 200 + 10% gives 220. Now let’s recover the rules for both + and ×, and try them.

One branch divides by 100. The other also multiplies by the first number. The agent uses both to recreate the % button.

› Use REA to inspect Windows Calculator’s % button. Recover the rules after + and ×, then build a small calculator that uses both.

Inspected with REA 4.1.0: Windows Calculator 11.2508.4.0, x64. The readable summary uses names from Microsoft’s public source to explain the recovered branch.

Percentage implementation · Microsoft’s test cases · Native setup guide

Download our Notes example, trace its CSV export, and check one changed input.

Tell your agent what you want to understand or build. With REA, you can work together on anything from cloning this website to reconstructing a game from its executable.

› Use REA to inspect https://rea.tools/. Clone this website for me.

› Use REA to reconstruct this game from its executable. Recover the gameplay logic in C and test it against the original.

Inspect functions, strings, references and call relationships in executables and libraries.

Map modules, routes, IPC and native dependencies from an application folder or ASAR archive.

Capture selected browser or process activity, then compare the results across runs.

Read the FAQ , chat with us on Discord , or open a GitHub issue for bugs and feature requests.

Share investigations and get help from other REA users on Discord. Follow REA on X for project updates.

items.title: Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected
items.summary: Fresh details reveal how the 40-year-old businessman flew and crossed regional borders while seriously ill.
items.content:
A Kenyan businessman was able to spend time in one of the regions worst-affected by Ebola, then travel to two more countries before his illness was identified.

The 40-year-old - who was only diagnosed with the deadly infectious disease after arriving seriously ill at a Nairobi hospital - became Kenya's first confirmed case. He died two days later on 5 October.

That his infection went undetected at multiple health facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and two airport health screenings in Uganda and Kenya has raised serious questions about these nations' biosecurity during a significant outbreak.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

Africa CDC, the continent's leading public health agency, has now reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements across nearly six weeks, revealing several missed opportunities to detect his infection and potentially preventing dozens of people from coming into contact with the deadly virus.

The account, presented by the agency's emergency director, Dr Wessam Mankoula, provides the clearest picture yet of how the businessman travelled thousands of kilometres while growing increasingly unwell.

The man, whose identity has not been made public, had lived in DR Congo for seven years and had travelled across three of its provinces on business.

Exactly when or where he contracted Ebola remains unclear - but it was present in all three provinces he went through by early October, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The man had spent much of late August and early September in the province of Bas-Uélé, visiting towns including Buta, Aketi and Likati.

The WHO confirmed an Ebola case in Buta in August, prior to his visit, though there is no evidence he contracted the virus there.

His symptoms first emerged around 15 September. He was given antibiotics and sent home.

Two days later, he was admitted to the Tongo Etandi Health Centre in Bondo, where he remained until 19 September.

Despite suffering from fever and a rash, he was diagnosed with a skin infection.

Without an Ebola test being taken at any point during his travels, it is hard to say exactly when he contracted the virus. Those symptoms are consistent with the early stages of the disease, but also other infections common to the region, such as malaria.

On 20 September, he flew to Kisangani, a city with a population of about 1.5 million people on the Congo River, where he spent more than 10 days seeking medical care.

We do not know which hospitals or clinics treated him there, nor what medications they gave him. Kisangani is the capital of Tshopo province which has only recorded 51 Ebola cases.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

Why Uganda is winning the battle against Ebola as virus spreads in DR Congo

However, on 1 October, more than two weeks after first becoming ill, the businessman boarded another domestic flight to Beni, before continuing his journey to Kasindi, a busy border town.

Both Beni and Kasindi are in North Kivu, which has recorded 1,755 Ebola infections and more than 1,000 deaths, making it one of the Congolese provinces worst-hit by the disease.

But he did not stay there long, crossing into Uganda later that day.

Uganda imposed restrictions on movement across its border with DR Congo shortly after the outbreak began in May.

The country has experience containing several Ebola outbreaks, including through surveillance, contact tracing and the isolation of suspected cases. It has had some cases this year - mostly among people travelling from DR Congo - but was declared free of the disease in August.

But the border between the two nations stretches for hundreds of kilometres through remote terrain, making it difficult to police.

It remains unclear whether the businessman passed through an official health checkpoint when he crossed the border.

Once he had, he travelled by road to the capital, Kampala, and then Entebbe International Airport, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi on 3 October.

Ugandan officials said his temperature was normal when he passed through airport screening. Health experts say his case highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

Mankoula said investigators were examining whether the man's medication could have suppressed his temperature. He may have also not had a fever when he passed through the checks.

Similarly, he was not flagged as a suspected Ebola patient when he reached Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, where a relative collected him and drove him directly to Nairobi Hospital, a private medical facility in the Kenyan capital.

By then, he was suffering from fever, chills, muscle pain, a sore throat and bleeding.

Laboratory tests confirmed that he had contracted the Bundibugyo species of Ebola - the same one responsible for the outbreak in DR Congo.

He was placed in isolation while his condition deteriorated. He died on 5 October and was buried the following day under strict infection-control measures.

The Kenyan government says it has now identified 66 people who may have been in contact with him after he arrived there. The WHO says the number is likely to rise as contact-tracing in Uganda and DR Congo continues.

The quarantine arrangements have also raised concerns among some healthcare workers, amid questions about how the patient was handled at Nairobi Hospital.

Kenya's health ministry says more than 652,000 travellers have been screened and nearly 5,000 healthcare workers trained to deal with Ebola, with five facilities designated to handle cases.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms, or through contaminated materials.

Its incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning someone exposed to the virus may not become ill until several weeks later.

Mankoula urged travellers experiencing symptoms of Ebola to report them, saying early medical attention could improve their chances of survival.

"When you reveal any Ebola-related symptoms early, you're not only preventing the virus spreading to other countries but you're also protecting yourself first," he said.

The WHO has warned that stigma surrounding Ebola could discourage people from reporting symptoms or seeking medical care, potentially allowing the virus to spread undetected.

The agency says it is stepping up efforts to encourage this by reducing fear and misinformation about the disease - something that is a big problem in DR Congo, where some health workers have been attacked by people who claim Ebola doesn't exist.

'I buried my parents one day after the other' - Ebola mourners learn how to grieve safely

Recovery of Ebola patients offers rare moments of joy at epicentre of outbreak

'They said it isn't real': Ebola rumours fuel attacks on health workers

items.title: Clinical trial of a prion disease drug candidate begins enrolling participants
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.broadinstitute.org/news/clinical-trial-prion-disease-drug-candidate-begins-enrolling-participants Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50028027 Points: 84 # Comments: 18
items.content:
It’s the first time the potential treatment, a small interfering RNA targeting the prion protein, is being tested in humans.

A new drug candidate designed to slow the progression of prion disease is entering a phase 1 clinical trial , which will evaluate the potential medicine for safety and tolerability.

Prion diseases are a class of neurodegenerative disorders that are caused by the accumulation of misfolded prion protein (PrP) in the brain. There are currently no cures, and the disease is fatal within months or years after symptoms begin. The new drug candidate, developed by Broad Institute and University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School scientists, is a small interfering RNA (siRNA) that binds and snips RNA molecules encoding the prion protein, reducing the amount of the disease-causing protein in the brain. Previous research in animals has shown that lowering prion protein levels can delay onset and slow down the disease. The trial, called PrP-targeting siRNA Safety & Mechanism Study (PRiSM), is enrolling patients exhibiting symptoms of the disease.

“To finally advance this drug to a human trial is the long-overdue achievement of a longstanding dream, but it's also the very beginning of learning about this drug's safety and activity in humans,” said Eric Minikel , principal investigator of the trial and codirector of Broad’s Prion Therapeutic Science program. “I am looking forward to finding out whether this candidate has a future as a drug in our disease, but no matter what the outcome, as sponsor-investigators, we will learn a lot about how to run a clinical trial in prion disease, and we plan to broadly and publicly share our data and findings to benefit all sponsors who want to develop drugs for prion disease.”

The drug candidate is a divalent siRNA: two identical siRNAs that are linked together and designed to distribute more broadly in the brain than single siRNAs. The divalent siRNA was developed at the UMass Chan Medical School by Anastasia Khvorova and her lab. Khvorova, Minikel, and Sonia Vallabh , codirector of Broad’s Prion Therapeutic Science program, have been working together since 2019 on developing an siRNA-based drug to target prion protein mRNA. Vallabh and Minikel, who are wife and husband, have dedicated their lives to creating a cure or treatment for prion disease, after learning in 2011 that Vallabh has the genetic mutation that causes the disease.

In March 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared the team’s Investigational New Drug (IND) application to start a clinical trial on this drug candidate — a document that is usually kept private by drug companies. However, Minikel and Vallabh published their IND filing publicly, and have committed to sharing new insights openly.

This green light from the FDA — a significant step in the drug development process — follows promising animal data from the Minikel/Vallabh lab. The scientists showed that a divalent siRNA lowered prion protein in mice by 49 percent and resulted in a 64 percent increase in survival time with a single dose after symptom onset. The study is published in Nucleic Acids Research .

The clinical trial is being supported by NeuroNEXT, or Network for Excellence in Neuroscience Clinical Trials, a program of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), a part of the National Institutes of Health. NeuroNEXT provides both funding as well as infrastructure to run the trial, including trial sites, a clinical coordinating center housed at Mass General Hospital’s Neurology Department, and a data and statistics center at the University of Iowa.

“Eric and Sonia are visionaries who are not only top-notch scientists, but have enormous ethical conviction. I’m honored to have an opportunity to work with them,” said Khvorova, professor in UMass’s RNA Therapeutics Institute and Program in Molecular Medicine. “Their commitment to transparency is paving a new path for running a clinical trial, so we’re not only advancing therapy for prion disease, it’s advancing the field as a whole.”

The initial phase of the trial will enroll 15 symptomatic patients who will each receive one dose of the siRNA by lumbar puncture, and new patients enrolled over the course of the trial will receive larger doses than patients enrolled earlier. The trial will also have an observational arm consisting of 15 additional participants who will not receive any treatment. Minikel says they hope to add pre-sympomatic participants in the future. They also plan to share safety data as soon as they are able.

“Standard drug development is, for all sorts of reasons, not well set up to be a learning system,” Vallabh said. “But we can’t afford to treat each shot on goal as a self-contained unit – everything needs to feed the mission. I wish the absolute best for this exact molecule, and I also know that however it performs in the clinic, this experience must move us forward. It’s our job to figure out how.”

This is now the second clinical trial that Vallabh and her team at Broad have helped to enable. The first one, initiated by Ionis Pharmaceuticals, began in 2023 for drug candidate ION717 and is ongoing. In their lab, Minikel and Vallabh are pursuing other possible therapeutic approaches for prion disease, including epigenetic and gene editing .

To learn more about PRiSM, visit ClinicalTrials.gov and CureFFI.org , where Minikel shares information for the prion patient and scientific communities. For patient resources, Minikel and Vallabh recommend visiting the CJD Foundation .

The drug development was funded by National Institutes of Health grants and by donations from members of the prion disease community to the Broad Institute and to Prion Alliance . This clinical trial is being funded by the National Institutes of Neurological Disorders and Stroke through the NeuroNEXT program (Grant 3OT2NS138339-01S2).

Gentile J, et al. Divalent siRNA for prion disease . Nucleic Acids Research . Online April 24, 2026. DOI: 10.1093/nar/gkag287

items.title: Compiling Rust to readable C with Eurydice
items.summary: Article URL: https://lwn.net/Articles/1055211/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027853 Points: 92 # Comments: 24
items.content:
A few years ago, the only way to compile Rust code was using the rustc compiler with LLVM as a backend. Since then, several projects, including Mutabah's Rust Compiler (mrustc), GCC's Rust support (gccrs), rust_codegen_gcc , and Cranelift have made enormous progress on diversifying Rust's compiler implementations. The most recent such project, Eurydice , has a more ambitious goal: converting Rust code to clean C code. This is especially useful in high-assurance software, where existing verification and compliance tools expect C. Until such tools can be updated to work with Rust, Eurydice could provide a smoother transition for these projects, as well as a stepping-stone for environments that have a C compiler but no working Rust compiler. Eurydice has been used to compile some post-quantum-cryptography routines from Rust to C, for example.

Eurydice was started in 2023, and includes some code under the MIT license and some under the Apache-2.0 license. It's part of the Aeneas project, which works to develop several different tools related to applying formal verification tools to Rust code. The various Aeneas projects are maintained by a group of people employed by Inria (France's national computer-science-research institution) and Microsoft, but they do accept outside contributions.

Eurydice follows the same general structure as many compilers: take a Rust program, convert it into an intermediate representation (IR), modify the IR with a series of passes, and then output it as code in a lower-level language (in this case, C). Jonathan Protzenko, the most prolific contributor to Eurydice, has a blog post where he explains the project's approach. Unlike other compilers, however, Eurydice is concerned with preserving the overall structure of the code while removing constructs that exist in Rust but not in C. For example, consider this Rust function that calculates the least common multiple of two numbers using their greatest common denominator:

Whether this C code counts as "readable" is probably a matter of individual taste. It does, however, preserve the structure of the code. Even the evaluation order of the original is preserved by adding extra temporary variables ( uu____0 in example_lcm() ) where necessary to define an order. (Rust guarantees that if the multiplication overflows and causes a panic, that will happen before any side effects caused by calling example_gcd() , but C only guarantees that if the multiplication is performed in a separate statement.) Compiling the same functions with rustc results in a pair of entangled loops filled with bit-twiddling operations, instead — which is appropriate for machine-code output, but much less readable.

Of course, not all Rust programs can be faithfully represented in C. For example, for loops that use an iterator instead of a range need to be compiled to while loops that call into some of Eurydice's support code to manage the state of the iterator. More importantly, C has no concept of generics, so Rust code needs to be monomorphized during conversion. This can result in several different implementations of a function that differ only by type — often, the more idiomatic C approach would be to use macros or void * arguments.

The implementation of dynamically sized types also poses certain challenges. In Rust, a structure can be defined where one of its fields does not have a fixed size — like flexible array members in C:

But if that structure is generic, and one of the generic users of the type gives the flexibly sized field a type with a known size, the compiler can take advantage of that knowledge to elide bounds checks where appropriate.

This kind of separation, where some parts of the code may know the size of a type and some may not, is an important semantic detail to preserve in C because of how it interacts with the possibility of formal verification. If Eurydice compiled DynamicallySized to use a flexible array member everywhere, analysis of the C code might point out "missing" bounds checks that were not required in Rust. Conversely, if Eurydice added extra bounds checks, it would need to manufacture extra error paths that don't appear in the Rust source and that should be completely unused.

So, Eurydice emits two different types: a version of the dynamically sized type that has a flexible array member, and one that has a known-length array member. Converting between the two representations is a no-op at run time, but it technically violates C's strict-aliasing rule. Therefore Protzenko recommends compiling Eurydice-generated code with -fno-strict-aliasing .

This approach, of compiling a more abstract language to C in a way that preserves the structure of the code, is not new. The KaRaMeL project, upon which Eurydice is based, does the same thing for the F* programming language. F* is a dependently typed functional programming language used to develop cryptographic libraries. Compiling provably correct F* programs to equivalent C lets those libraries be used in programs where performance is a concern.

Unfortunately, Eurydice doesn't currently scale much beyond small examples. Rather than implement its own parser and typechecker for Rust code, Eurydice uses another Aeneas tool — Charon — to extract the parsed and preprocessed program from rustc. When I tested Charon on a variety of Rust packages, it was routinely foiled by more recent Rust features such as const generics .

When Charon does work, however, it dumps rustc's medium-level intermediate representation (MIR) as JSON, along with any compiler flags necessary to understand the compilation. Eurydice reads this JSON representation and converts it to KaRaMeL's intermediate representation. Then it uses a series of small passes over the KaRaMeL code to eliminate some Rust-specific details, before handing things over to the same code-generation logic that KaRaMeL uses for F*.

In its current form, Eurydice works best for small, self-contained programs that avoid complex Rust features. Within that niche, however, it works well. The generated code maintains the same structure as the original Rust code, except for places where Eurydice emits extra intermediate variables or needs some glue code to implement a more complicated feature. On the other hand, small self-contained code is also the easiest to rewrite by hand, so bringing in Eurydice is probably only worthwhile if the original Rust code is going to be updated and one wants an automatic solution to keep them in sync. In any case, Eurydice is only the newest tool in a rapidly expanding collection of ways to fold, spindle, and mutilate Rust code to fit into more environments.

Regardless, if Eurydice is "routinely foiled by more recent Rust features" then it's nowhere near being able to compile rustc, which uses ~all the features, including many unstable ones. Rustc? If your goal is to minimize the number of binary dependencies, then you're better off using mrustc, which only requires a C++ compiler (which you probably already have as part of your bootstrap chain). In the bootstrappable.org/live-bootstrap case, they start from a small seed of commented machine code in hex encoding, that you can manually understand and write to a disk, then start the bootstrap. items.title: 'Everyone hates the police' – what France's school protests reveal about a divided nation
items.summary: Students taking to the streets have become a focal point in the country's increasingly polarised politics.
items.content:
As dustbins burn and students chant "everyone hates the police" in the French city of Lille, one teenager explains why he and his friends have taken to the streets.

"There aren't even enough chairs. We have to go and find some at the start of every lesson," the 16-year-old, who did not want to give his name, says of his school.

"We've got 50 minutes to eat at lunchtime but there are 2,000 of us that need to get through the canteen."

He is one of hundreds of thousands of students who have protested across France since the end of last month over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées, secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

Despite the government's apparent attempts to make concessions, the students show no sign of backing down.

"They have armies, they have the police, they have the powers," says Massicella, 18, as she marches through Lille. "But we have the mass population."

The protests, which have turned violent, have become a focal point in France's polarised politics, with all sides accusing the other of escalating tensions. As a presidential election approaches, politicians on both the hard right and hard left have sought to capitalise on the unrest and on what many see as the government's inability to resolve the crisis.

The protests - ignited at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in the deprived Paris suburb of Créteil - have struck a chord across the country.

Videos of rats scuttling through corridors in other lycées soon hit social media, providing striking symbols of the discontent. Other videos on TikTok and Instagram showed broken toilets, holes in walls and mouldy ceilings across the country. Students have complained of unbearable heat in the summer and freezing classrooms in the winter.

The anger has also focused on long school hours, chronic staff shortages, overcrowded classes and a deeply unpopular university admissions system.

The problem for the French government - which became clearer as we spoke to dozens of pupils this week - is that even if a tiny minority of schools have a problem with rodents, a very large number of pupils believe their own education is failing them.

On Tuesday, the government said 250,000 people marched, most of them young. The trade unions said it was more like half a million.

But it is not just students taking to the streets - their teachers are joining them.

Secondary school teacher Marine Monins, who joined the demonstrations in Lille, shows us a laminated timetable which she says illustrates the problem.

It has become normal for pupils to start at 8am and finish as late as 6pm, but the days are punctuated by hours-long gaps because of bad planning and staff shortages.

When lessons do go ahead, the classes are typically packed with 35 pupils (by comparison, the average secondary school class in England has fewer than 23 pupils).

"It's now impossible to give every child the attention they deserve," Monins explains.

On Thursday, the French government made its first sign of ceding ground to protesters, with a promise of 3,000 extra supply teachers in the coming days.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said by the end of October there will be a plan unveiled to respond to the crisis. Ministers have said they could look again at resources for schools within next year's squeezed budget.

But this has been met with a collective shrug at barricaded school gates across the country.

"It goes beyond having decent toilets in schools," lycée student Alcidor says in Paris, under the statue of Marianne at Place de la République, a place synonymous with protest.

"It's strong anger from the youth in France that doesn't feel represented, that feels abandoned, that feels unheard and is scared of what's coming in the future."

So far, almost 7,000 people have been detained during the disorder with more than 85% being children, according to the interior ministry.

More than 700 police officers have been injured in the past three weeks.

But rights groups and unions accuse the police of resorting to heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flash-ball guns. At least 200 pupils have been injured, along with dozens of teachers.

A 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a confrontation between police and demonstrators in the northern city of Lens.

Reports of how the teenager sustained the injury differ. A police union source cited by the AFP news agency said the boy appeared to have picked up a sting-ball grenade fired by riot police, which then exploded in his hand. However, a witness told local media that the teenager did not pick up the grenade.

A teacher at the boy's school, Bastien Riez, who is also a union rep, believes that current police tactics could irrevocably damage the relationship with France's youth.

"For many, this is their first experience of democracy and protest, and they are met with police and a sham of social dialogue and democracy. I fear that many young people will stop believing in this so-called democracy altogether."

Police have since been banned from using stun grenades at school protests.

But Parisian pupil Kaspar, 15, speaks of his fear when coming face-to-face with police in full riot gear. He says he and his friends have been protesting peacefully, but strangers were hijacking their protests.

"These people are coming just to shoot fireworks at police officers and they run. This is not the message we want to send to the world."

Police chiefs say violence, directed by agitators who have no link to the schools, is making their job incredibly hard.

Michel Chaballier, deputy secretary-general of the National Police Commissioners' Union (SCPN), says he fears the "political climate has been radicalised", and it was more and more difficult to have a calm, constructive public debate ahead of the national vote next spring.

"Police officers find themselves caught in the middle of this social tension, which is sometimes fuelled by irresponsible politicians," he says. "That's a shame, because I think this country deserves better."

The protests have become another bruising battleground in France's culture wars, with leaders of the hard left and right seeking to capitalise.

More than three-quarters of under-30s in France interviewed for an Ipsos survey conducted for Aix-Marseille University this week said they were worried about the state of their country.

But many people have a more profound and wider concern about just how dramatically the middle ground in France is eroding, leaving a chasm in the political landscape.

The education crisis is symptomatic of this but also threatens to act as an accelerant.

Most polling suggests more and more French citizens are looking to political extremes for answers to their problems – whether they are linked to education, the economy, identity or immigration.

Marine Le Pen of the hard right National Rally is the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race.

Next, neck and neck, are Édouard Philippe and Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

Philippe was a prime minister in President Emmanuel Macron's first term and has since founded a centre-right party called Horizons.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a veteran hard-left politician and founder of France Unbowed (LFI), has been a prominent older face among the students at rallies over the past three weeks.

Opponents have accused him of provoking and profiting from the unrest, while he counters that only his party truly represents the French youth.

He claims the current movement that has emerged from the schools protest is the most potent since 1968, when huge demonstrations almost brought down the government of President Charles de Gaulle. At its height, 10 million workers were on the streets before fresh elections led to the revolt fizzling out, but not before carving an indelible memory in French social history.

Despite being born more than four decades later, an exasperated generation of French teenagers are looking to the past for inspiration.

"I personally want to reproduce 1968!" Massicella declares in Lille, as she nears the end of the protest march.

Le Pen has stayed away from the protests and her most notable interventions have come in condemning the damage to schools, which is said to run into the millions of euros.

She has also suggested that parents of children who have committed the vandalism should pay for repairs.

The principle of casseur-payeur – those who break have to pay – has been an impassioned topic that has dominated French media this week.

The problem for President Macron is that there is no quick fix.

This is not a scenario where there is an unpopular piece of legislation that can be withdrawn in a hasty reverse ferret the prime minister is tasked with performing. That was the case with the gilets jaunes – the relentless protest in high vis jackets over a fuel tax rise nearly a decade ago.

Wholesale reform of the education system would cost billions – in new classrooms, new facilities, new teachers – and take years to achieve.

And changes that may seem more easily done – such as a reduction of the length of the school day – would be hugely problematic to implement logistically.

items.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
items.summary: The conservative commentator currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group.
items.content:
Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the US president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Trump called Zacharia "loyal" and "a devoted fan and member of MAGA" in a social media post on Friday, referring to his Make America Great Again movement, adding that she had "an unblemished record of support".

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

"She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7," Trump wrote on Truth Social of Zacharia.

"I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration."

Zacharia thanked him in a post on X, writing: "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime."

She said Trump had "shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day".

She said she looked forward "to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out".

The 42-year-old political strategist is a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News, and has been active in Republican politics for most of her adult life, having worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and for the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

Since June, she has been a senior communications adviser for Trump's media company and Truth Social platform, according to her LinkedIn profile. She worked in Homeland Security from February to March this year.

While she was only briefly in government at DHS - which the mother of four later said she left because of the strain of travel between California and Washington on her family - she has long been a ferocious defender of President Trump and his administration's policies.

In a June interview with the BBC , for example, she dismissed criticism of Trump's controversial use of the White House to host a televised UFC fight, saying the principles of the UFC "are the kind of principles that founded our Constitutional Republic".

"It's about not giving up the fight until the bitter end," she said. "I think there's no better summation of the American ethos than a good UFC fight."

Earlier this year, Zacharia wrote an op-ed in the New York Post about an incident in which she was asked to stop wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat to her local gym.

"I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," she wrote. "This is raw, unfiltered intolerance. Freedom of speech doesn't evaporate at the gym door."

Justin Buchler, a political science professor at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio, told the BBC that Trump's appointments during his second term have been "based on personal affiliation and loyalty".

"He values loyalty first and foremost," Buchler told the BBC.

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

In 2011, she spent nearly two years clerking at a law firm in Beijing, China.

Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

The complex job of press secretary goes beyond the briefing room podium to include managing contentious relationships with the press, coordinating with other parts of the White House, and providing media advice to the president. The secretary also oversees an office that receives a significant amount of inquiries and requests on a daily basis.

Yanna Krupnikov, a political scientist and professor of communication and media at the University of Michigan, said the selection of Zacharia "speaks to a blurring of the lines between different media types".

Politicians nowadays need to communicate not only to various news outlets but with people in a social media context, she said.

"I think the goal is not as much speaking to the media and journalists, but making sure that particular, very specific sound-bytes and messages get to ordinary people," Krupnikov told the BBC.

When Leavitt left the role, Trump called her one of his "most trusted aides", which sets a high bar for her replacement. Leavitt left because she said she wanted to spend more time with her family.

items.title: Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices
items.summary: The US president hopes to ease his party's pain before next month's midterm elections, writes the BBC's North America correspondent.
items.content:
Donald Trump's decision to import Russian fuel to the US represents a remarkable about-face from the president.

Just three weeks ago, Trump signed legislation to authorise fresh American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.

Now, Trump says, Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel to the US and world markets in the coming months.

The deal comes as Trump is still grappling with the political fallout of the Iran war and its impact on global energy prices, weeks before American voters head to the polls in the midterm elections.

As the cost of fuel has skyrocketed in America, his standing with the public – stung by the higher prices at the pump and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation – has soured.

The toll the war is taking has been acutely felt by US agricultural states, which rely heavily on diesel to operate farming machinery and to transport their products to market.

It is these states – places like Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Ohio – that have become unexpected political battlegrounds in the upcoming elections that will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress.

Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'

For months, the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain.

He recently pressured European allies to further tap their oil reserves . He deferred federal taxes on the fuel and authorised supplies designated for farm use to be used in interstate trucking.

He has also promised that he would not renew attacks on Iran until after the midterms – an unusually frank acknowledgement of the political impact the ongoing conflict is having.

His decision to strike a deal with Russia's Putin is only the latest, most dramatic effort.

Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information, of course. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return – besides much-needed hard currency – is unclear.

It opens Trump to criticism from European allies and American politicians that his administration is now helping to fund the Russian war machine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a "gift" to Putin that Russia would "repay" with "terror and perfidy".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on X.

It is also uncertain exactly how much Trump's move will help Republicans at the ballot box.

The promised European diesel release hasn't moved energy prices significantly, and there's no information on the speed with which Russian fuel could enter the market.

Its diesel refinery capacity has been damaged by repeated Ukrainian strikes – attacks that Trump has encouraged Zelensky to curtail.

The US uses approximately 3.6 million barrels of diesel a day, so even if Russia delivers its promised 300,000 tons this month, that amounts to approximately half of the US daily consumption.

With less than a month before November's midterm elections, early voting has already started in many states. The political cake, as the saying goes, is all but baked.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post.

But over the past seven months, prices on energy, fuel and consumer goods have only gone up - even as Trump and his officials have repeatedly assured an uneasy public a successful resolution to the war, and an easing of its economic impact, is nearly at hand.

Trump may be left hoping that his latest deal, setting aside its potentially uncomfortable diplomatic issues, will be enough to convince American voters that his promise of impending economic relief is more than just empty words.

Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?
